key_insight: Integrating vaccine trial records with a common data model and biomedical ontologies improved semantic retrieval and adverse-event ranking while supporting trial similarity analysis and design recommendations.
clinical_relevance: The framework could help researchers compare registered vaccine studies and inform trial planning, but it does not establish clinical safety or efficacy.
method: Mapped 9,147 AACT vaccine study records into SEA-CDM and linked vaccines and adverse events to VO and OAE.
Organized integrated records in relational tables and a Neo4j knowledge graph with links to original registrations.
Evaluated ontology-expanded search, adverse-event ranking, embedding-based trial similarity, and trial design recommendation.
evidence_signal: Ontology-expanded search retrieved 41 candidate RNA vaccine trials versus 16 with exact matching; adverse-event recall@10 rose from 0.317 to 0.383, and trial-similarity Hits@10 reached 0.950.
watch_item: Trial design recommendation performance varied across 23 vaccine classes under leave-one-Material-out evaluation, warranting further validation before use in trial planning.
paper_title: Ontology-Based SEA-CDM Integration for Vaccine Clinical Trials: Query, Similarity, and Design Recommendation
